closures.detour: Signed; Linn Cove Visitor Center closed
closures.reason: Great American Outdoors Act project (Linn Cove)

campgrounds.name: Waynesboro North 340 Campground
campgrounds.showers: Free hot showers, heated bathhouse — Good Sam rates restrooms 9.5/10
campgrounds.group: No formal group site; adjoining sites blocked on request
campgrounds.access: US-250 W into Waynesboro then US-340 N — 8.5 mi / 14 min from Rockfish Gap (MP 0).
campgrounds.standout: Cheapest verified hot-shower tent site at the north end and 14 min from where the Parkway meets Skyline Drive. Laundry, pool, pavilion.
campgrounds.watchout: Open RV-park field on US-340 — little shade or privacy, some road noise.
campgrounds.food: Waynesboro 5 min: Basic City Beer, Seven Arrows, Stable Craft.

campgrounds.name: Sherando Lake Rec Area (USFS)
campgrounds.showers: Free hot showers + flush toilets in all three loops; group bathhouse renovated 2019
campgrounds.group: YES — 5 tent-only group sites, up to 15 people, $50/night, own bathhouse
campgrounds.access: VA-664 from Reeds Gap (MP 13.7) — 3.8 mi / 11 min of steep twisty pavement.
campgrounds.standout: Closest real campground to the Parkway in the MP 0–30 stretch, with a tent-only group loop at $50 for up to 15 and its own shower house. Swimming lake to cool off in.
campgrounds.watchout: Zero cell service, no walk-ups — no reservation means no gate code, and the gate locks at 10pm.
campgrounds.food: None on site. Stock up in Stuarts Draft or Waynesboro (~20 min).

campgrounds.name: Devils Backbone Camp at Basecamp Brewpub
campgrounds.showers: 24/7 bath house, heated showers, free — reviewers repeatedly call them the cleanest they've used
campgrounds.group: YES — dedicated remote group tent site, up to 8 adults / 3 tents
campgrounds.access: VA-664 east from Reeds Gap (MP 13.7) to VA-151 — 6.6 mi / 10 min, all paved.
campgrounds.standout: Park the bike at the tent and walk to a full brewery restaurant. Sits on VA-151, the brewery/cidery corridor, 10 min off the Parkway.
campgrounds.watchout: Two-night minimum on weekends and the open hookup field has no shade — reviewers call it sweltering in midsummer.
campgrounds.food: Basecamp Brewpub on site; Bold Rock, Blue Mountain, Wild Wolf within 15 min.

campgrounds.name: Montebello Camping & Fishing Resort
campgrounds.showers: Free hot showers, one central bathhouse, cleaned daily
campgrounds.group: NO — one tent per primitive site, so a 4-rider group pays for 4 sites
campgrounds.access: VA-56 east from Tye River Gap (MP 27.2) — 3.0 mi / 6 min.
campgrounds.standout: Closest campground to the Parkway on the VA north half, on VA-56 between Tye River Gap and Crabtree Falls — arguably the best motorcycle road in central Virginia. Store, ice cream, 24-hr laundry.
campgrounds.watchout: One tent per site plus uneven gravel pads, and genuinely no cell service or usable WiFi.
campgrounds.food: On-site general store & ice cream (closes 6pm); VA-151 breweries ~30 min.

campgrounds.name: Glen Maury Park Campground
campgrounds.showers: Free bathhouse showers with hot water; each upper area has its own
campgrounds.group: YES in practice — big open rally fields used for festivals
campgrounds.access: US-60 west off the ridge into Buena Vista from MP 45.6 — 11.3 mi / 17 min. Good sweeper descent.
campgrounds.standout: 315-acre municipal park with open rally fields that absorb a 3–6 bike group without paying for six pads, one mile from town food and beer.
campgrounds.watchout: $55 for a tent site in a city field is steep, and after 4:30pm it's cash through a door slot.
campgrounds.food: Buena Vista 1 mi; Lexington 8 mi (Devils Backbone Outpost).

campgrounds.name: Jellystone Park — Natural Bridge
campgrounds.showers: Free hot showers and flush toilets in bathhouses, tent sites sited close to one
campgrounds.group: YES — group accommodations, call to arrange adjoining sites
campgrounds.access: VA-130 west from the James River access (MP 63.6) — 15.2 mi / 24 min, all paved.
campgrounds.standout: The only verified hot-shower option within 25 min of the James River crossing, and it has paved pads, laundry, camp store and snack bar — a good mid-tour resupply and laundry stop.
campgrounds.watchout: It's a kids' water-park resort — splash pads, activities and resort pricing, not a quiet moto camp.
campgrounds.food: On-site market and snack bar; Lexington 20 min.

campgrounds.name: Middle Creek Campground
campgrounds.showers: Hot showers and bathhouse on site
campgrounds.group: No formal group site; spacious creekside sites bookable adjacently
campgrounds.access: VA-43 north from Bearwallow Gap (MP 90.9) through Buchanan, then VA-614 — ~14 mi / 30 min. Take the paved route, NOT the shorter unpaved McFalls Creek Rd.
campgrounds.standout: The only shower-equipped camp near the Peaks of Otter stretch, and VA-43 from Bearwallow Gap down to Buchanan is a superb switchback descent to start the day on.
campgrounds.watchout: The access road itself — 2024–25 reviews describe potholes and a 'dangerous crevice.' Ride in slowly, in daylight.
campgrounds.food: Camp store on site; Buchanan 10 mi.

campgrounds.name: Explore Park / Don's Cab-Inns
campgrounds.showers: Keypad-code bathhouse, hot showers, private shower suites — reviewers say 'immaculate'
campgrounds.group: YES — group camping up to 15 (primitive) or 20 (drive-up)
campgrounds.access: ON the Parkway — turn off at MP 115 onto the Roanoke River Parkway spur, 1.5 mi in. Zero highway miles.
campgrounds.standout: Paved pads, a spotless keypad bathhouse and a brewpub on a 1,100-acre park you enter straight off the Parkway. Never touch a public highway.
campgrounds.watchout: No pets, little shade, only ~18 sites — fall weekends book far ahead, and the brewpub only opens Fri–Sat.
campgrounds.food: Twin Creeks Brewpub on site (Fri–Sat); downtown Roanoke 15 min.

campgrounds.name: Floyd / Blue Ridge Parkway KOA Holiday
campgrounds.showers: Modern bathhouses with hot showers; two ADA shower houses
campgrounds.group: YES — 200-acre former festival farm with event barn, amphitheater, pavilion; 30x30 pads take 6
campgrounds.access: VA-8 from Tuggle Gap (MP 165.3) via Floyd — 9.6 mi / 20 min.
campgrounds.standout: The most space on this list — a former bluegrass-festival farm with 30x30 pads and a pavilion, 13 min from the Floyd Country Store Friday Night Jamboree.
campgrounds.watchout: Grass-only pads on open farm field and the farthest from the Parkway here — a wet weekend means soft ground for sidestands. (Old chantillyfarm.com domain is now spam — don't use it.)
campgrounds.food: Downtown Floyd 6 mi — Dogtown Roadhouse, Buffalo Mountain Brewery.

campgrounds.name: Willville Motorcycle Camp
campgrounds.showers: Hot showers, multiple sinks, mirrors, hairdryer, soap & shampoo provided
campgrounds.group: YES effectively — no site boundaries, plus a free covered pavilion with grills and a community fire ring
campgrounds.access: US-58 west 3/4 mi from Meadows of Dan (MP 177.7). Owner warns: do NOT trust Google Maps, use GPS N36 44.012 W080 25.619.
campgrounds.standout: Motorcycle-only. No RVs, no generators, no families — just riders around a communal bonfire with free morning coffee, 4 minutes from Mabry Mill.
campgrounds.watchout: Old-school operation, dated site, no online booking — call before you commit a group. US-58 has active VDOT widening work.
campgrounds.food: Poor Farmer's Market <1 mi; Mabry Mill Restaurant MP 176; Chateau Morrisette MP 171.5.

campgrounds.name: Meadows of Dan Campground & Cabins
campgrounds.showers: 'Ultra-clean' bathhouse, hot showers
campgrounds.group: No dedicated group site; book 2 adjacent of the 12 tent sites
campgrounds.access: 0.3 mi west of the Parkway at the US-58 junction (MP 177.7) — 4 min.
campgrounds.standout: Full-service and year-round right at the Parkway junction, with electric and water at every tent site. The obvious shoulder-season base when Willville next door is closed.
campgrounds.watchout: Tent sites are up a hill at the end of the road and stay shaded and damp — soft ground and moss rather than a firm pad.
campgrounds.food: Poor Farmer's Market, Mabry Mill Restaurant, Chateau Morrisette; Floyd Country Store ~20 mi.

campgrounds.name: Fancy Gap / Blue Ridge Parkway KOA Journey
campgrounds.showers: Individual private bathrooms, each with shower/sink/toilet — 'spotless' with 'endless hot water'
campgrounds.rating: 5.0 The Dyrt (30) — 2025 VA Campground of the Year
campgrounds.group: YES — group camping; sites T84/T86 have covered kitchens plus a kitchen pavilion
campgrounds.access: 100 yards off the Parkway at US-52, Fancy Gap (MP 199.4) — 0.6 mi / 3 min.
campgrounds.standout: Gravel tent pad plus private lock-behind-you shower rooms is the most motorcycle-friendly hardware combo in Virginia, 100 yards off the Parkway, with BBQ delivered to your site.
campgrounds.watchout: Family KOA with pool and playground — expect kids, RV neighbors and peak-season rates above the mom-and-pop options nearby.
campgrounds.food: Dave's Smokehouse BBQ + camp store on site; Mount Airy 13 mi.

campgrounds.name: Fancy Gap Cabins & Campground
campgrounds.showers: Five private bathrooms, hot showers — 'strong pressure and reliable hot water'
campgrounds.group: 10% off when you book as a group; 5 tent sites total
campgrounds.access: Directly ON the Parkway — mailing address is 202595 Blue Ridge Parkway. Zero miles.
campgrounds.standout: You never leave the Parkway. Pull off at MP 202.5 into a gravel tent site with power and water, five private hot-shower bathrooms and laundry, for $36 all-in.
campgrounds.watchout: Only Tent 14 is drive-in — the other four require parking on the tent road and walking gear in, so a 4-bike group can't all park at their tents.
campgrounds.food: Lil' Camp Store on site; Fancy Gap 4 mi; Blue Ridge Music Center MP 213.

campgrounds.name: Old Cranks Campground & RV Park
campgrounds.showers: Hot showers in bathhouse (one reviewer notes the women's side is slow to warm)
campgrounds.group: Primitive tent field that absorbs Fiddlers' Convention crowds — fine for 3–6
campgrounds.access: VA-89 north into Galax from MP 215.8 — 7 mi / 15 min. 10 min to the Blue Ridge Music Center.
campgrounds.standout: The only walk-to-town option — park the bikes and walk to Galax breweries, restaurants and the Rex Theater. Vintage motorcar museum on the same property.
campgrounds.watchout: Small, plain in-town lot with limited office hours, no published tent rate and a tired bathhouse. Call ahead.
campgrounds.food: Walk to Creek Bottom Brews, Galax Smokehouse, Macado's; Rex Theater bluegrass Saturdays.

campgrounds.name: Stone Mountain State Park
campgrounds.showers: Hot showers in bathhouses on all three loops; B & C open year-round
campgrounds.season: B & C loops year-round; A loop closed Nov–Feb
campgrounds.group: YES — 4 walk-in group sites, up to 35 people, $75/night
campgrounds.access: US-21 south from MP 229.6 to Roaring Gap, then Oklahoma Rd — 8.4 mi / 21 min.
campgrounds.standout: Cheapest hot-shower option on the NC north end and the only one with real gravel tent pads plus paved loop roads. 90 sites means midweek availability even in October.
campgrounds.watchout: Group sites are walk-in, so you can't park bikes at the group site — book adjacent C-loop sites instead if that matters.
campgrounds.food: Country store near the entrance; Elkin 25 min, Sparta 30 min. No camp store inside.

campgrounds.name: Miller's Camping
campgrounds.price: $28 tent; +$10/night per extra tent on group site
campgrounds.showers: Hot showers in the public bath house (also serves MST hikers)
campgrounds.restrooms: Flush toilets, laundry in bath house
campgrounds.group: YES — group site priced per additional tent, good fit for 3–6 riders
campgrounds.access: Own access road off the Parkway via Stillhouse Branch Rd — literally 100 yards. 1 min.
campgrounds.standout: The best 'roll off the Parkway and stop riding' option in the corridor. Country store on site where campers gather for old-time music at night. Hot showers, laundry, WiFi, ice, firewood.
campgrounds.watchout: Closed Nov–Mar, and the website's booking flow is minimal — rates and policies really need a phone call.
campgrounds.food: On-site country store; The Bluffs at Doughton Park MP 241 (seasonal); Sparta 15 mi.

campgrounds.name: Raccoon Holler Campground
campgrounds.showers: Multiple bathhouses throughout the campground — reviewers single these out
campgrounds.group: Not advertised; adjacent sites bookable together
campgrounds.access: 1/4 mile west of the Parkway at MP 257.75, near Glendale Springs — 2 min.
campgrounds.standout: Paved roads to every site plus multiple bathhouses, laundry and a camp store — unusually well-appointed for a Parkway-adjacent camp, a quarter mile off the road.
campgrounds.watchout: Heavily seasonal/RV-oriented with lots of long-term campers, and no published tent pricing.
campgrounds.food: Glendale Springs adjacent; West Jefferson 10 mi for restaurants and breweries.

campgrounds.name: High Country Motorcycle Camp
campgrounds.showers: Renovated bath house with hot showers (confirmed on the operator's own site). Laundry is listed only by third-party directories — confirm by phone.
campgrounds.restrooms: Toilets in bath house; reviewers call them 'very clean'
campgrounds.season: Opens late Apr/early May — 2026 dates NOT confirmed online, CALL 336-973-3911
campgrounds.group: YES — pavilion seats 250 with a cowboy kitchen; hosts rallies regularly
campgrounds.access: US-421 at Deep Gap (MP 276) — 8.1 mi / 14 min direct, or the owner's preferred twisty 12-mi route. NOTE: Parkway MP 274.3–276.5 is closed for bridge repairs, detour signed from MP 269.8.
campgrounds.standout: Run by a BMW MOA ambassador explicitly for the two-wheel community — streamside tent camping, renovated bath house with showers and laundry, $20 a rider. Chalets have a lean-to that shelters two bikes.
campgrounds.watchout: The operator's site still advertises 2025 events and says 'call to check' — 2026 operation is unconfirmed online, so phone before you route a group here. Cell coverage on site is essentially nil on all carriers.
campgrounds.food: Firewood and ice only on site; Wilkesboro 15–20 mi.

campgrounds.name: Rider's Roost Motorcycle Resort
campgrounds.showers: Hot showers, modern bathrooms
campgrounds.season: Opens Apr 3, 2026; water drained early Nov
campgrounds.group: YES — call for group parties; bunkhouse by the bed; full 2026 event calendar
campgrounds.access: 19.5 mi / 30 min to Deep Gap (MP 276) — the farthest here, but every route in (incl. NC-268, a Scenic Byway) is a good ride.
campgrounds.standout: Motorcycle-only resort — no cars, no RV crowd — with level grassy tent sites on the waterfalls of Elk Creek, lockers, firewood and staff who'll lay out your day's ride. Recovered from Helene, running a full 2026 season.
campgrounds.watchout: No pets, and event weekends are deliberately loud parties — come midweek if you want quiet.
campgrounds.food: No on-site restaurant; Wilkesboro 15 mi. Alcohol permitted on site.

campgrounds.name: Flintlock Campground
campgrounds.showers: Hot showers
campgrounds.group: Call for groups of any size
campgrounds.access: On NC-105 between Boone and Foscoe — 8.1 mi / 17 min from the US-321 Blowing Rock access (MP 291.8).
campgrounds.standout: Best-rated conventional campground near Boone/Blowing Rock, with a creek through the property (ask for site 23), laundry, camp store, pool table and a fireplace lounge.
campgrounds.watchout: NC-105 road noise is the single most common complaint — request a site away from the highway side.
campgrounds.food: NC-105 toward Foscoe and Banner Elk; Boone 10 min for the full range.

campgrounds.name: Grandfather Campground
campgrounds.showers: Heated showers in bathhouses
campgrounds.group: YES — group rustic tent area for 8+, $25 site + $7 per person per night
campgrounds.access: On NC-105, 12.3 mi / 23 min to the US-221 Beacon Heights access (MP 305.2). Avoid Holloway Mountain Rd and Shulls Mill Rd — stay on US-321 to Boone then NC-105 south. NOTE: Parkway MP 304.4–305.1 closed for the Linn Cove project, detour signed.
campgrounds.standout: $20 rustic tent sites make this the cheapest hot-shower option near Grandfather Mountain, open year-round, with a store, laundromat and Watauga River fishing on site.
campgrounds.watchout: Site terrain is rocky and uneven in spots with protruding roots — pick your pitch carefully. Two-week max on tent sites.
campgrounds.food: NC-105 toward Foscoe and Banner Elk; Boone 10 mi. Store on site.

campgrounds.name: Linville Falls Campground (private)
campgrounds.showers: Hot showers; individual private bathrooms with showers; 'clean bathhouse' cited constantly
campgrounds.restrooms: Flush toilets, laundry with commercial machines
campgrounds.rating: 4.8 TripAdvisor (497) — highest-rated on this whole map
campgrounds.group: Pavilion for gatherings; book adjacent sites
campgrounds.access: US-221 at the Linville Falls community (MP 317.5) — 1.3–3.3 mi / 4–8 min. CRITICAL: the Parkway is Helene-closed southbound MP 317.5–327.5, so this is the end of the line heading south. Route out via US-221 or NC-181.
campgrounds.standout: The highest-rated campground anywhere on this map (4.8 from nearly 500 reviews), open and running normally while the NPS campground next door stays Helene-closed. Store, laundry, daily trash pickup at your site, monthly live music.
campgrounds.watchout: No internet and spotty cell — and the Parkway south of here is closed, so plan the detour before you arrive.
campgrounds.food: Well-stocked camp store on site; Newland 10 mi, Spruce Pine 15 mi.

campgrounds.name: Spacious Skies Bear Den
campgrounds.showers: Bathhouses described as 'amazingly clean and air-conditioned'
campgrounds.group: YES — Spacious Skies runs a group camping program
campgrounds.access: You CANNOT reach it on the Parkway — MP 317.5–327.5 is Helene-closed with recreation prohibited. Come via US-221 / NC-226 from Spruce Pine or Marion. From camp it's 4.9 mi / 11 min to the open Parkway at the Orchard at Altapass (MP 328.3).
campgrounds.standout: Reopened after major Helene repairs, now year-round with air-conditioned bathhouses, laundry, camp store, a private fishing/swimming lake and a waterfall trail. 600 acres inside the Pisgah NF boundary.
campgrounds.watchout: Surrounded by closed Parkway — MP 317.5–327.5 and MP 333.9–355.3 are both shut, so the Mount Mitchell/Asheville continuation is off the table for 2026.
campgrounds.food: Camp store on site; Spruce Pine 9 mi.

campgrounds.name: Asheville East KOA Holiday
campgrounds.showers: Hot showers in bathhouses fully reconstructed after Helene — newest wet facilities in the Asheville area
campgrounds.group: 32 tent sites, up to 6 people each — easy to block several
campgrounds.access: US-70 east from MP 382.6 (Oteen) — 10 mi / 17 min. Also I-40 Exit 59, 1 mi.
campgrounds.standout: Reopened Oct 2025 after a full Helene rebuild — brand-new admin building and bathhouse, 32 tent sites, camp store, laundry, pool.
campgrounds.watchout: I-40 and rail noise is the consistent complaint (the front desk keeps earplugs), and back-side sites were still being rebuilt in phases.
campgrounds.food: Black Mountain 6 mi — Pisgah Brewing, Foothills Butcher Bar; Ingles 2 mi.

campgrounds.name: Lake Powhatan Rec Area (Pisgah NF)
campgrounds.showers: Hot showers and flush toilets, individual timer-controlled stalls, bathhouse per loop
campgrounds.group: No dedicated group site — book 2–3 adjacent
campgrounds.access: NC-191 south from MP 393.6 then Bent Creek Ranch Rd — 4–5 mi / 10 min.
campgrounds.standout: Closest full-service showered campground to Asheville that's still national forest, with paved pads in the Lakeside Loop. Survived Helene operating year-round. Bent Creek trails start at the gate.
campgrounds.watchout: Reservations are online-only and Bent Creek is a mountain-bike destination — summer weekends sell out weeks ahead.
campgrounds.food: Sierra Nevada Brewing 15 min; Biltmore Village 10 min. Ice and firewood only on site.

campgrounds.name: Asheville West KOA Holiday
campgrounds.showers: Private hot showers
campgrounds.restrooms: Flush toilets, private shower rooms, laundry
campgrounds.group: Max 6 per tent site; adjacent sites bookable
campgrounds.access: 9 mi / 18 min from MP 393.6 via NC-191. Better: NC-151 from MP 411.8 at Candler — 11 mi of tight switchbacks straight to the door.
campgrounds.standout: Marketed by KOA specifically for riders, with its own motorcycle-camping guide. The gravel tent pad comes with a covered picnic table, a light and a charging station — a rider's setup.
campgrounds.watchout: Heavy I-40 noise and occasional paper-mill odor; KOA says follow their written directions, not GPS, for the last half mile.
campgrounds.food: Smokey Park Hwy strip 5 min; Sierra Nevada 25 min. Store on site.

campgrounds.name: Mount Pisgah Campground (NPS)
campgrounds.showers: Hot, COIN/FEE-OPERATED, in the Loop B and Loop C bathhouses (open to all loops)
campgrounds.restrooms: Flush toilets, comfort station per loop, drinking water
campgrounds.group: No dedicated group site — book adjacent tent-only sites in Loops C/D
campgrounds.access: Entrance road is directly off the Parkway at MP 408.6. Zero non-Parkway miles.
campgrounds.standout: The only campground actually ON the Parkway in NC with hot showers, at 4,980 ft. Paved parking spur at every site plus a separate framed tent pad. Pisgah Inn restaurant, store and laundromat half a mile away.
campgrounds.watchout: Showers are coin-operated and only in Loops B/C, cell service is nonexistent, and it fills on summer and fall weekends.
campgrounds.food: Pisgah Inn restaurant + country store + laundromat, 0.5 mi. Nothing else within 15 twisty miles.

campgrounds.name: Moonshine Creek Campground
campgrounds.showers: Multiple bathhouses, hot showers, heated restrooms — reviewers say 'immaculate' and 'pristine'
campgrounds.group: YES — group sites offered, call for 3–6 rider blocks
campgrounds.access: 2.5 mi / 7 min from Balsam Gap (MP 443.1) via Dark Ridge Rd. DO NOT USE GPS — the campground warns nav apps route you down an old logging road. Use their written directions.
campgrounds.standout: 2.5 miles off the Parkway at 2,887 ft with a trout creek through camp, a country store, laundry and near-perfect bathhouse marks — the best-rated option in the Balsam/Waynesville stretch.
campgrounds.watchout: Strict two-night minimum on all tent bookings with non-refundable deposits, and several creekside sites are walk-in only (bike stays in the lot).
campgrounds.food: On-site country store; Sylva 10–15 min (Innovation Brewing); Waynesville 15 min.

campgrounds.name: Lake Junaluska Campground
campgrounds.showers: Hot showers in the bathhouses
campgrounds.restrooms: Flush toilets, ADA bathroom, on-site laundromat
campgrounds.group: No formal group site; tent sites are close together, fine for 3–6
campgrounds.access: 9 mi / 15 min from Balsam Gap (MP 443.1) via US 74-23, or 11 mi / 20 min from Soco Gap (MP 455.7) down US-19 through Maggie Valley.
campgrounds.standout: Cheapest verified hot-shower tent camping in the Waynesville/Maggie Valley corridor, with raised gravel tent pads and free campers' access to the Conference Center pool and lakeside trail.
campgrounds.watchout: US-19 traffic noise is the most repeated complaint — reviewers call it horrendous on the highway-side sites. Ask for a back site.
campgrounds.food: US-19 restaurants at the door; Waynesville 4 mi (Boojum, Frog Level Brewing); Maggie Valley 7 mi.

campgrounds.name: Cherokee / Great Smokies KOA Holiday
campgrounds.showers: Hot showers in bathhouses adjacent to the tent loop
campgrounds.restrooms: Flush toilets, multiple bathhouses, laundry, camp store
campgrounds.group: Tent sites hold 6; adjacent sites bookable as a block
campgrounds.access: From the southern terminus at US-441, 2 mi south then 3 mi up Big Cove Rd — 5 mi / 10 min.
campgrounds.standout: The last (or first) campground on the Parkway's south end with real hot showers, on the Raven Fork with tribal trout ponds. Practical basecamp before Newfound Gap, the Cherohala or Deals Gap.
campgrounds.watchout: Multiple tent campers report road noise and inconsistent hot water, plus mud after heavy rain — request a pond-side no-hookup site.
campgrounds.food: Camp store on site; Cherokee 5–10 min (Granny's Kitchen, Harrah's restaurants).

campgrounds.name: Iron Horse Motorcycle Lodge & Resort
campgrounds.price: $35.99 tent (no electric, 1 person) / $42.99 w/ electric; +$8 per extra guest
campgrounds.showers: Washrooms, hot showers, dressing rooms and laundry; shampoo and soap provided
campgrounds.group: YES — explicitly equipped for large groups; bunkhouse and Conestoga wagons too
campgrounds.access: Deals Gap tack-on — ~50 mi / 1hr15 west of the terminus via US-74 to NC-28. Sits between the Tail of the Dragon, NC-28 'Hellbender' and the Cherohala Skyway.
campgrounds.standout: Purpose-built motorcycle-only resort since 2003 — the Chuck Wagon Grill does breakfast daily and dinner Tue–Sat, plus covered bike parking, fuel, bike wash, loading ramp, pool tables, giant ride maps on the lodge walls and a fire pit that becomes the nightly rider debrief.
campgrounds.watchout: 2024–26 reviews flag reservation and phone problems (one main line reported disconnected) — confirm your booking by a second channel before you ride out.
campgrounds.food: Chuck Wagon Grill on site — breakfast daily, dinner Tue–Sat; Robbinsville 10–12 mi.

campgrounds.name: Kickstand Lodge Motorcycle Campground
campgrounds.showers: Hot showers with 'fabulous' pressure; towels, hairdryers, shampoo, razors and soap free in the shower house
campgrounds.restrooms: Flush toilets, men's and women's bathhouse, laundry service
campgrounds.group: YES — per-person pricing plus covered pavilions and a bunkhouse make it the cheapest way to put 3–6 riders together near the Dragon
campgrounds.access: Deals Gap tack-on — ~48 mi / 1hr10 west of the terminus via US-74 to NC-28 at Stecoah Valley. Minutes from Fontana Dam, the Dragon and the Cherohala.
campgrounds.standout: Per-person pricing at $25 with a shower house stocked like a hotel bathroom — towels, hairdryer, toiletries. Bike wash and free tire air on site.
campgrounds.watchout: Small operation with a thin recent review trail — call ahead to confirm they're taking campers on your dates.
campgrounds.food: Stecoah Valley deli minutes away; Robbinsville 10 mi; grills and BBQ areas on site.

places.name: Cherokee / Great Smokies KOA Holiday
places.access: From the southern terminus at US-441, 2 mi south then 3 mi up Big Cove Rd — 5 mi / 10 min.
places.standout: The last (or first) campground on the Parkway's south end with real hot showers, on the Raven Fork with tribal trout ponds. Practical basecamp before Newfound Gap, the Cherohala or Deals Gap.
places.watchout: Multiple tent campers report road noise and inconsistent hot water, plus mud after heavy rain — request a pond-side no-hookup site.
places.food: Camp store on site; Cherokee 5–10 min (Granny's Kitchen, Harrah's restaurants).

places.name: Iron Horse Motorcycle Lodge & Resort
places.price: $35.99 tent (no electric, 1 person) / $42.99 w/ electric; +$8 per extra guest
places.access: Deals Gap tack-on — ~50 mi / 1hr15 west of the terminus via US-74 to NC-28. Sits between the Tail of the Dragon, NC-28 'Hellbender' and the Cherohala Skyway.
places.standout: Purpose-built motorcycle-only resort since 2003 — the Chuck Wagon Grill does breakfast daily and dinner Tue–Sat, plus covered bike parking, fuel, bike wash, loading ramp, pool tables, giant ride maps on the lodge walls and a fire pit that becomes the nightly rider debrief.
places.watchout: 2024–26 reviews flag reservation and phone problems (one main line reported disconnected) — confirm your booking by a second channel before you ride out.
places.food: Chuck Wagon Grill on site — breakfast daily, dinner Tue–Sat; Robbinsville 10–12 mi.

places.name: Kickstand Lodge Motorcycle Campground
places.access: Deals Gap tack-on — ~48 mi / 1hr10 west of the terminus via US-74 to NC-28 at Stecoah Valley. Minutes from Fontana Dam, the Dragon and the Cherohala.
places.standout: Per-person pricing at $25 with a shower house stocked like a hotel bathroom — towels, hairdryer, toiletries. Bike wash and free tire air on site.
places.watchout: Small operation with a thin recent review trail — call ahead to confirm they're taking campers on your dates.
places.food: Stecoah Valley deli minutes away; Robbinsville 10 mi; grills and BBQ areas on site.
